problem:

$$
x=2u-v,\,y=3u+2,\,z=u+2v
$$

for $0\le u\le 1$ and $-1\le v\le 1.$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Surface Area of a Parametric Surface
examples.problem:
Find the surface area of the parametric surface defined by the equations 

$$
x = u, \quad 
y = v, \quad 
z = 1 - u - v
$$

for $-1 \leq u \leq 1$ and $0 \leq v \leq 3.$
examples.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $\mathbf r (u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface area of $S$ is given by

$$
\iint\limits_S \,\textrm d S = \iint\limits_D  \left\|  \mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v \right\|  \text{d}A.
$$

In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
\mathbf{r}(u,v) = \left\langle u, \: v, \: 1 - u - v \right\rangle.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(1-u-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,-1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(1-u-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,1,\,1⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and its magnitude is

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨1,\,1,\,1⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+1+1} \\  & =\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, let's denote

$$
D = \{ (u,v) \: : \: -1 \leq u \leq 1, \: 0 \leq v \leq 3\}.
$$

Then, the surface area is

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{3}\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{3}{∬}_{D}\text{ }\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{3}\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =\sqrt{3}\cdot 2\cdot 3 \\  & =6\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
$$
{∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A,\,D={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 2,\,0\le v\le 2}
$$

The integral above gives the surface area of the parametric surface $r(u,v)=⟨{u}^{2},\,u-{v}^{2},\,{v}^{2}⟩$ for $0\le u\le 2$ and $0\le v\le 2.$ What is the missing expression?
feedback.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface area of $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u-{v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({v}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨2u,\,1,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u-{v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({v}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-2v,\,2v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2u & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2v & 2v\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -2v & 2v\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}2u & 0 \\ 0 & 2v\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}2u & 1 \\ 0 & -2v\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨2v,\,-4uv,\,-4uv⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨2v,\,-4uv,\,-4uv⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{(2v)^{2}+(-4uv)^{2}+(-4uv)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{v}^{2}+16{u}^{2}{v}^{2}+16{u}^{2}{v}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{v}^{2}+32{u}^{2}{v}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{v}^{2}(1+8{u}^{2})} \\  & =\sqrt{4{v}^{2}}\sqrt{1+8{u}^{2}} \\  & =2v\sqrt{1+8{u}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $\sqrt{{v}^{2}}=v$ since $v\ge 0$ on $D.$

Therefore, the surface area is

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2v\sqrt{1+8{u}^{2}}\,\text{d}A\end{aligned}
$$
